submissions.findingTextShort: A bipolar-depression RCT showed endpoint disagreement rather than a uniformly positive antidepressant result.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 24917198 randomized 80 adults with bipolar depression to adjunctive pregnenolone, titrated to 500 mg/day, or placebo for 12 weeks. A treatment-by-week interaction favored pregnenolone on the clinician-rated HRSD but not the self-rated IDS-SR; remission also differed depending on which scale was used. The evidence should therefore remain endpoint-specific and adjunctive-treatment specific rather than being collapsed into a general mood or antidepressant claim.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with bipolar disorder in a depressed mood state receiving adjunctive treatment
submissions.usageContext: Disease-specific adjunctive psychiatric treatment, not general wellness or everyday mood enhancement
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Clinician-rated and self-rated depression endpoints did not agree, and remission conclusions also depended on the scale used.

submissions.findingTextShort: An eight-week schizophrenia RCT found no significant improvement in the primary cognitive composite with pregnenolone.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 25030803 randomized 120 participants with schizophrenia after a placebo lead-in and found no significant pregnenolone-versus-placebo change in the MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery composite over eight weeks. This primary cognition null result must remain visible and must not be replaced by mechanistic neurosteroid plausibility or by improvement on a separate functional-capacity endpoint.
submissions.populationContext: Participants with schizophrenia receiving adjunctive pregnenolone or placebo
submissions.usageContext: Schizophrenia cognition endpoint; not healthy-person cognitive enhancement
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Functional capacity and cognition were separate prespecified outcomes and cannot be treated as interchangeable evidence of cognitive benefit.

submissions.findingTextShort: The same schizophrenia RCT reported a functional-capacity signal despite the null cognition composite.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In PMID 25030803, pregnenolone was associated with greater improvement in the UPSA-B functional-capacity composite than placebo while the primary MCCB cognition composite remained null. The functional-capacity signal is therefore a distinct disease-specific endpoint and cannot be relabeled as proven cognitive enhancement, generalized to healthy users, or used to erase the cognition null result.
submissions.populationContext: Participants with schizophrenia in an eight-week adjunctive randomized trial
submissions.usageContext: Functional capacity in schizophrenia, separate from cognitive performance and generic wellness
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The positive functional-capacity endpoint coexists with a null cognition composite and requires disease, duration and adjunctive-treatment boundaries.
